questions.prompt: A plugin injected with ['session', 'llm'] is running. The plugin providing llm unloads. What happens?
options: The plugin keeps running with a stale llm
The plugin is unloaded, and is mounted again once llm is provided again
The kernel throws because a needed service disappeared
Only the plugin's llm calls fail; everything else continues
questions.explanation: The watcher sees a missing need and unloads the plugin. When llm is provided again, the watcher mounts a fresh copy.

questions.prompt: A plugin declares it needs 'tools', but no plugin ever provides that name. What does the learner see?
options: The plugin runs with tools set to undefined
Nothing: the plugin waits forever without any message
The kernel creates an empty tools service
questions.explanation: inject only starts the plugin when every need exists. A name nobody provides keeps it waiting silently, which is a common trap.

questions.prompt: Why does load order stop mattering once plugins use inject?
options: Because every change to the shelf re-runs the watchers, which start a plugin as soon as its needs appear
Because the kernel sorts plugins alphabetically before mounting
Because get() waits until the service exists
Because provide() refuses to run until all plugins are mounted
questions.explanation: provide and its disposer both call changed(), so a waiting plugin is checked again every time the shelf changes, whatever order things were mounted in.
